 NBA’s injury crisis impacts Warriors-Timberwolves matchup 
 Anthony Edwards will not play, while Yaxel Lendeborg’s status is up in the air

 By Joseph Dycus | jdycus@bayareanewsgroup.com | Bay Area News Group PUBLISHED: October 27, 2026 at 4:34 PM PDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... MINNEAPOLIS – The injury bug running rampant early this NBA season bit the Warriors and Timberwolves before the teams’ Wednesday matchup.
 ESPN reported that Minnesota superstar Anthony Edwards will undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee and could miss up to two months.
 Edwards joins Paolo Banchero, Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace, Jalen Duren, Jaren Jackson Jr., Lauri Markkanen and Jalen Suggs as high-profile players who have sustained serious injuries over the first week of the season.
 Meanwhile, star Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg showed up on the injury report as questionable with inflammation in his left foot.
 Lendeborg limped to the Warriors’ podium after their win over the Nuggets in Denver on Monday night, and later told reporters at his locker that he had stepped on his own foot.
 “Now it’s just tender in my left foot, and it was stupid, man,” Lendeborg said. “But (the Warriors’ medical staff) said it should be nothing crazy.”
 Fans could be deprived of watching two of the more captivating personalities in the league.
 Edwards is a four-time All-Star who helped knock the Warriors out of the 2025 postseason in a second-round series.
 He had gotten off to a torrid start to this season, averaging 33.3 points per game while thriving next to new additions LaMelo Ball and Jonathan Kuminga for the 3-1 Timberwolves.
 Meanwhile, Lendeborg has been an undeniable bright spot for the Warriors. He etched his name next to a pair of Warriors legends in Monday’s 134-114 victory over the Nuggets, the team’s first win of the season.

 Lendeborg’s 13 free-throw attempts were the most by a Warriors rookie since Curry dropped in 12 foul shots and scored 40 in the final game of his rookie season back in 2010. And his 87 points through four games were the highest total by a Warriors rookie since Wilt Chamberlain, who had 150 in 1959.
 The rookie has endeared himself to his veterans by asking incessant questions and being a “sponge” while also gaining notoriety among the NBA fanbase at large for his candid remarks to reporters.
 Lendeborg leads the Warriors in minutes played at 133, with Gui Santos a distant second at 96. On a Warriors team replete with older players who require load management – Steph Curry, Draymond Green, Al Horford – head coach Steve Kerr has repeatedly said he expects Lendeborg to lead the team in minutes.
 But now he might not suit up, at least for a game.
 What should have been a premier matchup of the night will be missing at least one of the primary figures when the game tips off at 5 p.m. Pacific Time.
